newsitem.title: INDIA: India plans 5-8 pct rise in fuel prices - daily.
newsitem.headline: India plans 5-8 pct rise in fuel prices - daily.

text.p: India is preparing to unveil next week a package of reform measures in the oil sector involving a five to eight percent rise in the prices of petrol, diesel and kerosene, the Business Standard said on Tuesday.

The daily said India also planned to dismantle the state-controlled administered pricing mechanism (APM) for petroleum prices by 1999/2000 (April-March) and abolish by 1998/99 the policy that allows imports only by state firms.
The package involves a phased reduction of import duties on crude oil and petroleum from 1998, it said.

The policy-making Steering Committee of the ruling United Front coalition is scheduled to meet on July 2 to take a final decision on fuel price hikes, opposed by leftwing partners. The meeting had initially be set for Friday.

Officials have been pushing hard for a fuel price hike to contain a burgeoning oil pool deficit, or debt owned by the government to state oil companies, estimated at 155 billion rupees ($4.3 billion) at the end of March.
At its last meeting on June 16, the United Front postponed a decision on whether to raise fuel prices.
The Economic Times said on Monday that the government was considering imposing a "windfall tax" on oil companies as part of a package to rein in the mounting costs.
The Business Standard said the government proposed a surcharge on the profits of oil companies benefiting from the deregulation of prices until the oil deficit was bridged.
The government also proposed to decontrol the distribution of petroleum products and abolish state licences required to operate in the oil sector, the newspaper said.
